We covered this space science researcher’s earlier efforts to rekindle this archaic computer memory tech back in February of this year.多分世界初！？USBフラッシュならぬUSB磁気コアメモリにテキストファイル入れてPC間の移動に成功！これで完成〜 128バイトだから動画の文字数くらいが限界笑 来週9/5-6のMaker Faire Tokyo 2026(有明GYM-EX)で展示・実演します！ pic.twitter.
bangla_paragraph2: com/sptsOYZUMpAugust 29, 2026ফেব্রুয়ারিতে আমরা লক্ষ্য করেছি যে এই ইউএসবি ফ্ল্যাশ ড্রাইভের কিছু গুরুতর ত্রুটি ছিল, তবে এটি একটি প্রচেষ্টা ছিল যা আমরা আন্তরিকভাবে প্রশংসা করেছি। এই অযৌক্তিক ইউএসবী ফ্ল্যাश ড্রাইভে তিনটি মূল অসুবিধা ছিল। প্রথমত, এটি বেশ বিশাল, এবং এটি প্রায় এক ফুট (30 সেমি) বর্গক্ষেত্রের মতো দেখাচ্ছে। দ্বিতীয়ত, এর বিপরীতে, এর স্টোরেজটি কেবল 128 বাইটে অবিশ্বাস্যভাবে ক্ষুদ্র (জিবি, এমবি বা এমনকি কেবি নয়) । অবশেষে, আমাদের প্রযুক্তির বোঝার মতে, সংরক্ষিত ডেটা  এর সময় মুছে ফেলা হয়।
bangla_paragraph3: টুইট-ইম্বডেড ভিডিওতে আমরা দেখতে পাচ্ছি যে নামহীন ইউএসবি টাইপ-এ গ্যাজেটটি তার যাদু কাজ করে। আকর্ষণীয়ভাবে, যখন @ ডিড্ট_নাওর ডিভাইস থেকে / থেকে ডেটা পড়া হয়, তখন সংযুক্ত 32 x 32 অ্যারেতে এলইডি একটি উজ্জ্বল লাল রঙের আলোকিত হয়। প্রতিটি এলইড একটি পৃথক চৌম্বকীয় কোরকে প্রতিস্থাপন করে। আমরা উইন্ডোজকে ড্রাইভটি 6.5 কেবি ক্ষমতা হিসাবে রিপোর্ট করতে দেখি, তবে এটি সম্ভবত রাস্পবেরি পাই পিকোকে একটি বোর্ড কন্ট্রোলার হিসাবে ব্যবহার করার সাথে সম্পর্কিত।
bangla_paragraph4: ভিডিওর শেষে আমরা দেখতে পাচ্ছি যে পাঠ্যটি ড্রাইভ থেকে নোটপ্যাডে সফলভাবে স্থানান্তরিত হয়েছে। কেবলমাত্র পাঠ্য ডেমো দিয়ে সন্তুষ্ট না হয়ে, @ ডিড্ট_নাও একটি বিএমপি চিত্র স্থানান্তরের সাথে অনুসরণ করে। এই ডিভাইসে 32 x 28 পিক্সেল পর্যন্ত একরঙা বিটম্যাপ সংরক্ষণ করা যেতে পারে। সম্ভবত সীমিত ডিভাইস মেমরির স্থান (32 x 4) চিত্র ফাইলের শিরোনাম দ্বারা ব্যবহৃত হয়। 3 এর চিত্র 1 আপনি আমাদের নিবন্ধে চৌম্বকীয় কোর মেমোরি সম্পর্কে আরও পড়তে পারেন যা এর পেটেন্ট ফাইলিংয়ের 75 তম বার্ষিকী উদযাপন করে
bangla_paragraph5: চৌম্বকীয় কোর মেমরি দুই দশক ধরে ডিজিটাল কম্পিউটারে এলোমেলো অ্যাক্সেসের স্টোরেজের প্রভাবশালী রূপ হিসাবে তার জায়গা অর্জন করেছে। আজ এটি একটি অদ্ভুত কৌতূহল বলে মনে হচ্ছে। গুগল নিউজে টম হার্ডওয়্যার অনুসরণ করুন, অথবা আমাদেরকে আপনার ফিডে আমাদের সর্বশেষ সংবাদ, বিশ্লেষণ এবং পর্যালোচনা পেতে আমাদের পছন্দসই উত্স হিসাবে যুক্ত করুন। টম'স হার্ডওয়ারের সেরা সংবাদ এবং গভীর পর্যালোচনার সরাসরি আপনার ইনবক্সে পান।

title: Welcome to Night Vale cocreator Joseph Fink learned storytelling from Grim Fandango
title_bn: নাইট ভ্যালির সহ-স্রষ্টা জোসেফ ফিনক গ্রিম ফান্ডাঙ্গোর কাছ থেকে গল্প বলার শিক্ষা নিয়েছেন।
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Joseph Fink is the cocreator and cowriter of Welcome to Night Vale, arguably the most important fiction podcast ever. He's also the creator of the noir podcast Unlicensed and Alice Isn't Dead, which takes some of the conspiratorial cosmic horror of N
paragraph1: Joseph Fink is the cocreator and cowriter of Welcome to Night Vale, arguably the most important fiction podcast ever. He’s also the creator of the noir podcast Unlicensed and Alice Isn’t Dead, which takes some of the conspiratorial cosmic horror of Night Vale and turns it into fodder for a more serious series about relationships, trauma, and the open road. There’s also a sequel series out now called Don’t Tell Alice that takes the story down an even darker path in which protagonist Keisha is the one with a secret.Joseph is also an accomplished author. In addition to co-writing the three Welcome to Night Vale novels, he’s also penned the Alice Isn’t Dead novel and The Halloween Moon. His latest work is The Nudge, which features some gorgeous illustrations from Jessica Hayworth, who also provides the art for Night Vale, hits shelves on September 1st. It’s a brief and unsettling novella about a man trying to outrun some mysterious evil.What is the first app you install on a new phone or computer?
paragraph2: Podcast Addict. It’s an Android-only podcast app made by one guy named Xavier, and it is so much better than any other podcast app that it’s the main reason I can never switch to an iPhone. I’m maybe the one guy in the entire country who chooses phones based on how they play podcasts.Which social media platform do you use the most?I use Bluesky, which I used to like because no one was there and so no one read my posts, which is really the ideal social media for me. Now there are more people there, and sometimes people read and respond to my posts, which is a drag.What game do you have the fondest memories of?My entire understanding of storytelling is probably shaped by Grim Fandango, a 1999 adventure game about a sad sack grim reaper navigating a film noir afterlife.
paragraph3: There are lines and images from that game that will live in my head forever, even if a lot of them were parodies or references to classic films I wasn’t even aware existed when I first played that game.What creation are you most proud of?Our Audible show Unlicensed was one of those few projects that turned out exactly how I wanted it to in my head. A mystery series set in the least cool parts of Los Angeles, the parts where the actual people live. I didn’t want it to be “good for two writers who usually don’t write mysteries.” I just wanted us to write a damn good mystery, and I think we did. We got three seasons out of Audible, but then they mostly shut down their original shows department, and that was it. If I had my choice though, I’d happily spend the rest of my life writing Unlicensed.
paragraph4: What’s the best piece of advice you’ve ever received?I recently watched a talk with Meshell Ndegeocello, and she described having to shush a fellow student in a guitar workshop who was noodling on his guitar while the teacher was trying to demonstrate something. Meshell said: “As a musician, it doesn’t matter how well you play if you can’t listen.” I don’t know if it’s the best advice I’ve ever received, but I think it’s damn good advice and applies to a lot of things outside of music.What’s the last piece of physical media you bought?I buy too many books, constantly. I like to hang out in bookstores, and I’ve never left one without buying at least a couple of books. I’m mostly not a physical media guy, I have no interest in owning records or DVDs, but I’ll build an addition to my house before I get rid of any books.
paragraph5: What would the tagline for your biopic be?“It turns out watching a guy write audio fiction on his computer is boring, this movie was a mistake sorry, we’re sorry.”What’s the last GIF or meme you used? I don’t really use GIFs or memes. I’m very much a text guy, which is why I stick to text social media mostly, even though that doesn’t really help you sell books or stuff like that.Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.
bangla_paragraph1: জোসেফ ফিনক হলেন ওয়েলকাম টু নাইট ভেলের সহ-প্রণেতা এবং সহ-লেখক, সম্ভবত সর্বকালের সবচেয়ে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ কল্পকাহিনী পডকাস্ট। তিনি নোর পডক্যাস্ট আনলাইসেন্সড এবং অ্যালিস ইজ না ডেডেরও স্রষ্টা, যা নাইটভেলের ষড়যন্ত্রমূলক মহাজাগতিক ভয়াবহতার কিছু গ্রহণ করে এবং এটিকে সম্পর্ক, ট্রমা এবং উন্মুক্ত রাস্তা সম্পর্কে আরও গুরুতর সিরিজের জন্য খাদ্যে পরিণত করে। এখন একটি সিক্যুয়েল সিরিজও রয়েছে ডনট টেল অ্যালিসের নামক যা গল্পটিকে আরও অন্ধকার পথে নিয়ে যায় যেখানে নায়ক কেশা হলেন
bangla_paragraph2: পডকাস্ট অ্যাডিক্ট। এটি একটি অ্যান্ড্রয়েড-কেবল পডক্যাস্ট অ্যাপ যা জ্যাভিয়ার নামে এক ব্যক্তি তৈরি করেছেন, এবং এটি অন্য যে কোনও পডকোস্ট অ্যাপের চেয়ে অনেক ভাল যে এটি প্রধান কারণ আমি কখনই আইফোনে স্যুইচ করতে পারি না। আমি সম্ভবত পুরো দেশে এমন এক ব্যক্তি যিনি পডকেস্টগুলি কীভাবে খেলেন তার ভিত্তিতে ফোনগুলি বেছে নেন। আপনি কোন সামাজিক মিডিয়া প্ল্যাটফর্মটি সবচেয়ে বেশি ব্যবহার করেন?আমি ব্লুজকি ব্যবহার করি, যা আমি পছন্দ করি কারণ কেউ সেখানে ছিল না এবং তাই কেউ আমার পোস্টগুলি পড়েন না, যা আমার জন্য সত্যিই আদর্শ সামাজিক মিডিয়ার। এখন সেখানে আরও বেশি লোক রয়েছে।
bangla_paragraph3: এই গেম থেকে কিছু লাইন এবং ছবি আছে যা আমার মাথায় চিরকাল বেঁচে থাকবে, যদিও তাদের অনেকগুলি ছিল প্যারোডি বা ক্লাসিক্যাল চলচ্চিত্রের উল্লেখ যা আমি প্রথম যখন এই গেমটি খেলেছিলাম তখনও জানতাম না। আপনি কোন সৃষ্টির জন্য সবচেয়ে বেশি গর্বিত?আমাদের শ্রবণযোগ্য শো অনলাইসেন্সড ছিল সেই কয়েকটি প্রকল্পের মধ্যে একটি যা আমার মনের মধ্যে ঠিক যেমনটি আমি চেয়েছিলাম ঠিক তেমনই পরিণত হয়েছিল। লস অ্যাঞ্জেলেসের সবচেয়ে কম শীতল অংশে একটি রহস্য সিরিজ, যেখানে প্রকৃত মানুষ বাস করে। আমি চাই না এটি দুই লেখকের জন্য ভাল হোক যারা
bangla_paragraph4: আপনি যে পরামর্শটি পেয়েছেন তা সবচেয়ে ভাল পরামর্শ কি?আমি সম্প্রতি মেশেল নেদেগোসেলোর সাথে একটি বক্তৃতা দেখেছি, এবং তিনি বর্ণনা করেছিলেন যে একজন সহকর্মীকে গিতার কর্মশালায় চুপ করিয়ে দিতে হয়েছিল যিনি তার গিটারটি তার গিতারে নডলিং করছিলেন যখন শিক্ষক কিছু প্রদর্শন করার চেষ্টা করছিলেন। মেশাল বলেছিলেনঃ একজন সংগীতশিল্পী হিসাবে, আপনি যদি শুনতে না পারেন তবে আপনি কতটা ভাল খেলেন তা গুরুত্বপূর্ণ নয়।আমি জানি না এটি আমার প্রাপ্ত সেরা পরামর্শ কিনা, তবে আমি মনে করি এটি একটি দুর্দান্ত পরামর্শ এবং সংগীতের বাইরে অনেক কিছুর জন্য প্রযোজ্য।
bangla_paragraph5: আপনার জীবনী ছবির ট্যাগলাইন কি হবে?এটা দেখা যাচ্ছে যে একজন লোক তার কম্পিউটারে অডিও ফিকশন লেখার সময় বিরক্তিকর, এই ছবিটি একটি ভুল ছিল দুঃখিত, আমরা দুঃখিত.আপনি সর্বশেষ কোন জিআইএফ বা মেম ব্যবহার করেছেন? আমি আসলে জিআইফ বা মেমের ব্যবহার করি না। আমি খুব বেশি পাঠ্য লোক, এজন্য আমি বেশিরভাগ সামাজিক মিডিয়াতে টেক্সট করি, যদিও এটি আপনাকে বই বা এর মতো জিনিস বিক্রি করতে সাহায্য করে না।আপনার ব্যক্তিগতকৃত হোমপেজে ফিডে এবং ইমেল পেতে এই গল্পের বিষয় এবং লেখকদের অনুসরণ করুন।

title: The Theragun Sense makes everyday recovery surprisingly easy
title_bn: থেরাগুন সেন্স প্রতিদিনের পুনরুদ্ধারকে সহজ করে তোলে।
author: TechPulse
excerpt: As my 20s are set to come to an end later this year, I’ve officially reached the age where sleeping in the wrong position or stretching just a little too far can cause aches and pains. I’ve always been somewhat skeptical of massage guns, mostly becau
paragraph1: As my 20s are set to come to an end later this year, I’ve officially reached the age where sleeping in the wrong position or stretching just a little too far can cause aches and pains. I’ve always been somewhat skeptical of massage guns, mostly because I’ve tried a few off-brand ones and just assumed they’d eventually end up collecting dust in a drawer. But after a few weeks of testing the Therabody Theragun Sense (2nd Gen), I was surprised. Turns out massage guns aren’t as gimmicky as I had thought. The Theragun Sense, which retails for $299, is a wellness-focused massage gun that’s designed for everyday aches, muscle tension, relaxation, and soreness. It’s more of a gentle massaging and relaxation tool rather than a hardcore recovery massage gun. If you’re looking for more of a deep-tissue massage, it might be worth checking out the Theragun PRO or Prime.
paragraph2: But if you don’t need a super heavy-duty massage gun with features like heated therapy and deep- tissue capabilities, the Theragun Sense is a great option for everyday use. My favorite thing about the massage gun is that it features built-in visually guided routines. The device comes with four routines, and you can access additional routines through the Therabody app and sync your favorite ones to the device using Bluetooth. Image Credits:Therabody / The Theragun Sense has an LCD screen that walks you through routines step by step. Once you select a routine, the screen shows you exactly where to use the massage gun, how long to spend on each area, and how much pressure to apply. As someone who never really had an idea of what to do with a massage gun other than pointing it to a sore muscle and hoping for the best, I liked that the Therabody Sense takes a lot of the guesswork out of using a massage gun. My favorite routine was the six-minute “Sleep” routine that’s essentially a quick full-body massage to get you ready for the night.
paragraph3: The app lets you choose from many other routines, like “Pre-Walk Warm-up,” “Desk Relief,” “Lower Back Recovery,” and more. The massage gun features five speeds to fine-tune pressure to allow for a more relaxing touch, moderate pressure, or a deeper tension release. I liked having the flexibility to change the intensity depending on how sore I was feeling that day. Since the device is designed to be lightweight, I found it easy to hold and get to those spots on my back and shoulders that are harder to reach. Image Credits:Therabody / For people who want more personalization, the Therabody app takes the guided experience a step further with Coach, the company’s AI feature that creates personalized recovery recommendations based on your goals and activity. Coach can recommend which part of your body to target, which settings or attachments to use, and when to fit a recovery session into your day. The relatively quiet motor was another feature I appreciated, as I could easily use the device while watching TV or relaxing without the sound of the massage gun acting as a distraction.
paragraph4: The Theragun Sense comes with a USB-C charging cable, a travel pouch, and two massage attachments: the Standard Ball and the Dampener, which is designed to target knots and tender areas. Separately, you can purchase the “Supersoft” attachment for $35 for extra sensitive areas on the body. Overall, the Theragun Sense (2nd Gen) won me over. It’s easy to use, comfortable to hold, and notably takes the guesswork out of using a massage gun. At $299, it isn’t cheap, but I think it’s a great option for people who want an everyday wellness device that can help them relax and recover. title: Top Stories: Apple's 'Surprise and Shine' Event, Plus New Mac mini and Mac Studio

excerpt: It turned out to be a big week for Apple news this week, as we not only got an official announcement about the upcoming iPhone event but also several hardware announcements including updated Mac mini and Mac Studio models. Anticipation continues to b
paragraph1: It turned out to be a big week for Apple news this week, as we not only got an official announcement about the upcoming iPhone event but also several hardware announcements including updated Mac mini and Mac Studio models. Anticipation continues to build for Apple's first foldable iPhone coming at next month's event, while subscribers to the Apple TV streaming service are getting hit with another price increase, so read on below for all of the details. Top Stories Apple Event Announced for September 9: 'Surprise and Shine' Apple this week announced that it plans to hold its annual iPhone-centric event on Wednesday, September 9, at the Apple Park campus in Cupertino, California. The event will begin at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time, with select members of the media invited to attend. The September 2026 iPhone event comes with the tagline "Surprise and Shine" and should see Apple announce the iPhone 18 Pro, the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, and the foldable iPhone, which could be called the iPhone Ultra. There won't be an iPhone 18 this year because Apple is waiting until spring 2027 to launch the more affordable models. Apple Announces New Mac Mini With M6 and M5 Pro Chips and More Apple this week announced the next-generation Mac mini, which can be configured with an all-new M6 chip or the M5 Pro chip released earlier this year. The M6 chip is equipped with a 12-core CPU and a 12-core GPU, up from a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU in the M5 chip.
paragraph2: In addition, the M6 chip features the first-ever dual Neural Engine with two 16-core engines, up from one in previous chips. The M6 chip has up to 170GB/s memory bandwidth, up from 153GB/s for the M5 chip. Apple said the Mac mini with the M6 chip delivers up to 40% faster CPU performance, up to 4× faster performance for AI tasks in particular, up to 2× faster graphics performance, and up to 2× faster storage speeds compared to the previous-generation model with the 10-core M4 chip, 32GB of unified memory, and 2TB of storage. Apple Unveils New Mac Studio With M5 Max and M5 Ultra Chips Alongside the updated Mac mini, Apple also announced new Mac Studio models with the M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips, the latter of which is the company's most powerful chip ever. The new ‌Mac Studio‌ features a next-generation SSD architecture built on PCIe Gen 6 that Apple says is up to twice as fast as before. The machine also gains Thunderbolt 5 ports with up to 120Gb/s of bandwidth, along with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 for the first time via Apple's N1 chip. The new ‌Mac Studio‌ also supports genlock over USB-C and can drive up to eight displays. The M5 Ultra chip includes an up to 36-core CPU that contains 12 super cores and 24 performance cores. It delivers up to 1.25x higher single-threaded performance and up to 1.
paragraph3: 3x higher multithreaded performance than the M3 Ultra from the previous generation ‌Mac Studio‌. Apple Releases New Polishing Cloth Apple this week also updated one of its most meme-worthy products in recent years, with a new version of its Polishing Cloth. It might be just a hint softer and thinner, and it's priced at just $9, half the price of the original one. Most of Apple's Magic Keyboards for Mac also got updates for the U.S. English versions this week, replacing text labels on edge keys like tab, caps lock, shift, return, and more with glyphs. Gurman: iPhone Ultra Wows Early Testers, Except for Its Camera Apple's upcoming foldable "iPhone Ultra" is winning over the few people who have had hands-on time with the device, though the camera setup may leave some users wanting, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. Writing in his latest "Power On" newsletter, Gurman says people who have used the device – which is reportedly referred to internally as the iPhone Ultra – like how it fits in your pocket, as well as the feel and durability of its hinge mechanism. Testers have also apparently praised the new iPad-like app layouts that take advantage of the larger internal display when the phone is unfolded. Beyond productivity, video, and gaming, Gurman says Apple's foldable device also performs well as a camera viewfinder.
paragraph4: However, the device lacks a telephoto lens, which could cost Apple some sales given the expected price. Apple TV Streaming Service Receives Price Increase For the fourth time since its launch, Apple has increased the price of its Apple TV streaming service in the United States, raising monthly pricing by $2 and annual pricing by $20 starting today. As a result of the Apple TV price increase, the Apple One Individual bundle has also gone up in price. Apple TV (Monthly): $14.99 per month (up from $12.99 per month) Apple TV (Annually): $119 per year (up from $99 per year) Apple One (Individual): $21.95 per month (up from $19.95 per month) Apple TV also received a price increase in Brazil, Chile, and Mexico today, according to Apple, but no other countries are affected in this round of increases. title: Nvidia’s AI advantage is moving beyond the GPU
title_bn: এনভিডিয়ার এআই সুবিধা জিপিইউর বাইরে চলে যাচ্ছে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The new generation of data center systems is increasing efficiency with smarter traffic control instead of just more processor cycles.
paragraph1: Before this week, the dominant story about Nvidia went something like this: For the first few years of the AI boom, Nvidia was the only source for state-of-the-art GPUs, which became immensely profitable as the industry scaled out. In the last few years, hyperscalers like Amazon and Google have started building their own chips, and Nvidia is no longer the only game in town, leading many investors to wonder how durable its advantage really is. It’s a compelling story, and mostly true. After growing its market cap 10x between the start of 2023 and mid-2025, Nvidia shares have been on a more modest trajectory for the past year, driven by concerns about GPU competition. A new narrative has taken shape since the company’s earnings on Wednesday and investors are starting to realize that Nvidia’s advantage goes far beyond GPUs. As AI’s compute grows into the gigawatt scale, orchestration has become an increasingly complex task. Not surprisingly, Nvidia has built much of the state-of-the-art hardware needed to handle it, giving the company a huge advantage in the systems that surround the GPU even as it sees increased competition on the GPUs themselves. For all the talk of compute as a commodity, it’s still incredibly difficult to operate a megascale data center at peak efficiency — and as deployments get bigger and faster, that challenge is only growing.
paragraph2: Rack by Rack You can see some of this just by looking at the details of what Nvidia is actually selling. The company is currently rolling out its Vera Rubin architecture, which pairs the Rubin GPU with a collection of other units, including the Vera CPU, the Groq 3 LPX inference accelerator and similar racks for storage and networking. Over the past week, I’ve been talking to folks at Nvidia about what those systems actually do, and the results have been surprising. Like the Rubin GPU itself, they’re extremely specialized systems, but instead of churning through tokens, they’re making sure everything outside the GPU works as efficiently as possible. If the GPU is the engine, these are the rest of the car. The Vera CPU in particular is focused on the problem of orchestrating data. “Vera is important because there’s only so much memory that you can put in a single server or any sort of compute platform,” Jason Hardy, Nvidia’s VP of storage technology, told me. As data centers have scaled up computing power, memory capacity has scaled up too, which is why companies like Micron have gotten rich in the second wave of the infrastructure boom.
paragraph3: But getting that data to the GPU at the right time isn’t straightforward — and as companies look to drive tokens-per-watt lower and lower, they’re realizing how important that kind of traffic direction is. “We saw upwards of 3x improvement in these operations, where the Vera CPU is allowing for acceleration,” Hardy said. “So now we can use our flash to its fullest potential, because we can get all that performance out of it without bottlenecking.” You can see versions of the same problem outside of Nvidia. When OpenAI developed its Jalapeño chip, a major focus was avoiding these challenges entirely by minimizing the amount of data that needs to be moved around. “We designed Jalapeño to minimize data movement and communication delays,” the company said in a blog post earlier this month. “Its large domain allows the entire workload to remain within one connected system, minimizing data movement and helping the complete request stay fast and efficient from beginning to end.” It’s a different approach, avoiding data movement entirely by conducting a workload within one integrated chip.
paragraph4: But the overall logic is the same, increasing efficiency with smarter traffic control instead of just more processor cycles. That in turn opens up a whole new layer of infrastructure for companies to compete over. This new focus on data orchestration isn’t automatically a win for Nvidia. The company will have to compete with rival chipmakers and hyperscalers just as it has with GPUs. But the competition has moved to a new layer, where building a rival GPU matters less than being able to make the entire system work efficiently. And at least in the early stages, Nvidia looks to have a commanding lead. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. This doesn’t affect our editorial independence.

He previously worked at The Verge and Rest of World, and has written for Wired, The Awl and MIT’s Technology Review. He can be reached at russell.brandom@techcrunch.com or on Signal at 412-401-5489.

title: The Galaxy Z Flip 8 is at its best when there’s friction
title_bn: গ্যালাক্সি জেড ফ্লিপ ৮ এর সেরা সময় হয় যখন ঘর্ষণ হয়
author: TechPulse
excerpt: What do you want from a flip phone when it's closed? A simple interface, perhaps notifications and a widget or two, for handling the basics? Or a fully fledged Android experience shrunk down for the Flip form factor? For years, Samsung has insisted o
paragraph1: What do you want from a flip phone when it’s closed? A simple interface, perhaps notifications and a widget or two, for handling the basics? Or a fully fledged Android experience shrunk down for the Flip form factor? For years, Samsung has insisted on the former, even as some fans — and Razr rival Motorola — have pushed for the latter. With the Galaxy Z Flip 8, Samsung has given in.Although the Z Flip 8’s hardware is almost unchanged year-on-year, Samsung has fundamentally rethought how this phone is meant to be used when shut. The cover screen feels more like a regular Android phone, with easier access to the full versions of every single app, letting you browse social media, watch movies, and play games without ever opening the phone. Not every app works well on a tiny square screen with two cameras in the middle of it, but even when they don’t, that friction between me and the distractions of my phone still feels as much a feature as a bug.8Verge Score$1200The GoodRuns any app on the cover screenThinner and lighterReliable batteryThe BadMostly a rehash of last year’s phoneStill vulnerable to dust$100 more expensive than the Z Flip 7Everything exciting about the Z Flip 8 lies in its 4-inch cover screen, which is now more versatile than ever thanks to a homescreen redesign. Swiping down from the top left now brings up your notifications, while swiping from the top right instead shows a cover-screen-optimized version of the Quick Settings panel. Immediately, this feels more like a phone.More exciting is what happens when you swipe up from the bottom: you get an app drawer. By default, this is populated with a selection of Samsung’s own apps that are optimized for the square screen, plus a “Labs” section with third-party options including Netflix and WhatsApp. But right below that, Samsung has included an easy prompt to install MultiStar, the Good Lock module that lets you run any app you’d like on the outer screen.Samsung used to bury the option deep in the phone’s settings, only to be found by those who knew to look for it.
paragraph2: The bottom of the app drawer isn’t quite front and center, but it’s much more prominent than it used to be.You can run any app you’d like on the cover screen.The Withings app scales badly: The graph takes up too much space to even show both axes, and it becomes impossible to scroll past it.Google Maps works, but it’s busy and awkward, especially when you try to zoom in.HBO Max works flawlessly, but it wouldn’t be my first choice to watch Lanterns.You can still run apps in three forms: full-screen, with the cameras blocking part of the software; a square display that stops just above the level of the cameras; or a thin portrait-aspect ratio that letterboxes the sides. A small virtual button at the bottom of the screen lets you cycle through them.Good performance isn’t guaranteed. Some apps, like Withings’ health tracker companion app, are almost impossible to use on the cover screen, with no configuration that leaves enough space for its graphs to fit. Google Maps is only a bit better — I love the idea of quickly checking my walking route without opening the phone, but there are so many floating interface elements that it’s unwieldy at best. Others work smoothly, but feel pointless: I can stream HBO Max on the tiny outer display, but I’d never want to.But for other apps, the new cover screen options feel genuinely freeing. I can open Todoist and tick off a task, dip into WhatsApp to send a message, or open MyFitnessPal to log the snack I just ate. They’re quick actions that work well enough on the small screen, and because other apps — *cough* Instagram *cough* — don’t, I can dive into them without the risk of getting dragged into doomscrolling. That little bit of friction is just enough to save me from wasting 20 minutes I’ll never get back.
paragraph3: Like last year’s phone, the cover screen wraps around the cameras.As for the hardware, little has changed. The Z Flip 8 is 0.6mm thinner and 8g lighter than its predecessor. This is the thickest of Samsung’s three current foldables, but it’s more compact than Motorola’s Razrs, its only real rivals.Samsung didn’t upgrade the Z Flip 8 with the thinner, tougher titanium display stack found in the two new Z Fold 8 phones, which also means this has just as visible a crease as ever. It rarely bothers me, and is hard to see head-on, but you may feel differently. The IP48 rating is a more objective issue, and means that while this phone is mostly safe from water, it’s still vulnerable to dust.On the inside, you’ll find the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 if you’re in the US, though my UK model runs Samsung’s Exynos 2600. Exynos chips get a bad rep, but performance has been smooth so far, and I have no real complaints.This is the online-exclusive mint, but the phone’s also available in pink, cream, and gray.It’s a little thinner and lighter than before, but not by much.And the crease is still pretty noticeable compared to the two new Fold 8 phones.As with the Z Fold 8 phones, Samsung switched to more energy-dense silicon-carbon batteries for the Z Flip 8. Unlike those phones, it didn’t actually increase the battery capacity, but instead used smaller cells with the same 4,300mAh capacity — the key to shrinking the phone itself.
paragraph4: Still, battery life is solid, reliably lasting the full day with battery to spare. The charging — 25W wired, 15W wireless — is relatively unimpressive, and the only way to get Qi2 charging is still by using a compatible magnetic case.Storage and RAM remain the same as on the Z Flip 7; the screens do too apart from small bumps to peak brightness, and the cameras are also identical to last year’s. The 50-megapixel main camera is impressive, and especially helpful since the form factor means you can use it for selfies too. The 12-megapixel ultrawide and 10-megapixel inner camera aren’t remarkable, but they get the job done. A slab phone at this price would have better cameras, and most likely a telephoto lens, but the lenses here are good enough.1/13The main camera mostly gets good results.The question is whether it’s all good enough for the price, given Samsung has bumped the Z Flip 8 up to $1,199.99, a $100 increase. Z Flip 7 owners certainly shouldn’t upgrade, and anyone else should consider buying that phone instead, since the difference between the two is slight.After all, the big upgrades are software, and unlikely to remain exclusive. Last year’s Z Flip 7 hasn’t yet been updated to One UI 9, but since its outer screen is almost identical, it seems likely to get the upgraded software, giving one less reason to opt for the new model. The Z Flip 6 and earlier, with their smaller cover screens, seem more likely to miss out. I’ve asked Samsung about its upgrade plans, but haven’t yet heard back.Customizable Now Brief cards were added in One UI 9.
paragraph5: The camcorder-inspired video recording is still one of the phone’s best features.If you find the full apps frustrating, various cover screen widgets are still available.Most of the other software upgrades aren’t even Flip-specific. Customizable, AI-powered cards have been added to the daily Now Brief; My FanCam lets you crop video to focus on a specific subject; and Audio Eraser can now dim background noise and highlight dialogue in apps like YouTube and Netflix. You’ll find those features across all of Samsung’s new foldables, plus the new Galaxy S26 FE.Modest as the Z Flip 8’s hardware upgrades are, it feels like a turning point for Samsung, which is mostly done trying to limit the ways people use the cover screen. Given the speculation that the short, wide Z Fold 8 could replace the Flip form factor as Samsung’s “small phone that unfolds to a big phone,” it makes sense to close the gap between them.The Z Fold 8 is definitely bigger than the Z Flip 8.But the Flip’s small, obstructed screen is less functional — for better or worse.Open, the Z Fold 8 feels like a compact tablet.While the Flip opens up to a pretty regular phone.

bangla_paragraph2: অ্যাপ্লিকেশন ড্রয়ারের নীচে খুব সামনে এবং কেন্দ্রে নেই, তবে এটি আগের চেয়ে অনেক বেশি বিশিষ্ট।আপনি কভার স্ক্রিনে আপনার পছন্দ মতো যে কোনও অ্যাপ্লিকেশান চালাতে পারেন।উইথিংস অ্যাপ্লিকেসনটি খারাপভাবে স্কেল করেঃ গ্রাফটি উভয় অক্ষ দেখানোর জন্যও খুব বেশি জায়গা নেয় এবং এটির পাশ দিয়ে স্ক্রোল করা অসম্ভব হয়ে পড়ে।গুগল ম্যাপস কাজ করে, তবে আপনি যখন জুম করার চেষ্টা করেন তখন এটি ব্যস্ত এবং অস্বস্তিকর।এইচবিও ম্যাক্স নিখুঁতভাবে কাজ করে তবে এটি আমার প্রথম পছন্দ হবে না ল্যান্টার্নস দেখতে।আপনার এখনও তিনটি ফর্মের অ্যাপ্লিকেেশন চালাতে পারবেনঃ পূর্ণ-স্ক্রিন
bangla_paragraph3: গত বছরের ফোনের মতো, কভার স্ক্রিনটি ক্যামেরাগুলিকে ঘিরে রাখে। হার্ডওয়্যার হিসাবে, সামান্য পরিবর্তন হয়েছে। জেড ফ্লিপ 8 এর পূর্বসূরীর চেয়ে 0.6 মিমি পাতলা এবং 8 গ্রাম হালকা। এটি স্যামসাংয়ের বর্তমান তিনটি ভাঁজযোগ্যগুলির মধ্যে সবচেয়ে পুরু, তবে এটি মটোরোলার রেজারের চেয়ে কমপ্যাক্ট, এর একমাত্র বাস্তব প্রতিদ্বন্দ্বী। স্যামসুং জেড ফ্লাইপ 8 কে দুটি নতুন জেড ফল্ড 8 ফোনে পাওয়া পাতলা, শক্ত টাইটানিয়াম ডিসপ্লে স্ট্যাকের সাথে আপগ্রেড করেনি, যার অর্থ এটির আগের মতো দৃশ্যমান ভাঁজেরও রয়েছে। এটি খুব কমই বিরক্ত করে

bangla_paragraph5: ক্যামকর্ডার অনুপ্রাণিত ভিডিও রেকর্ডিং এখনও ফোনের সেরা বৈশিষ্ট্যগুলির মধ্যে একটি।আপনি যদি সম্পূর্ণ অ্যাপ্লিকেশনগুলি হতাশাগ্রস্ত মনে করেন তবে বিভিন্ন কভার স্ক্রিন উইজেটগুলি এখনও উপলব্ধ।অন্যান্য বেশিরভাগ সফ্টওয়্যার আপগ্রেড এমনকি ফ্লিপ-নির্দিষ্ট নয়। কাস্টমাইজযোগ্য, এআই-চালিত কার্ডগুলি দৈনিক এখন সংক্ষিপ্তে যুক্ত করা হয়েছে; আমার ফ্যানক্যাম আপনাকে একটি নির্দিষ্ট বিষয়ে ফোকাস করার জন্য ভিডিও ক্রপ করতে দেয়; এবং অডিও ইরেজার এখন ব্যাকগ্রাউন্ড গোলমাল ম্লান করতে এবং ইউটিউব এবং নেটফ্লিক্সের মতো অ্যাপ্লিকেশানগুলিতে ডায়লগ হাইল করতে পারে। আপনি এই বৈশিষ্ট্যগুলি অ্যাক্রোসে পাবেন।

title: Gemini Spark is almost a dream AI assistant — except for 1 thing Perplexity does better
title_bn: জেমিনি স্পার্ক প্রায় স্বপ্নের এআই সহকারী  তবে এক জিনিস ব্যতীত পারপ্লেক্সিটি আরও ভাল করে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Using Perplexity Computer extensively revealed exactly how limited Gemini Spark is.
paragraph1: Karandeep Singh / Android AuthorityI seriously thought this day would be far out in the future, but here we are. We already have AI assistants that can take instructions and execute a series of tasks (not just one at a time) without your supervision — it’s almost like having a human assistant.Google’s Gemini Spark is one such product. In fact, it’s one of the first of its kind to be so easily and widely accessible to end users rather than enterprises. It’s so intuitive that I instinctively gravitate towards Spark whenever I need something done within the Google ecosystem. It’s supposed to work in the background, but I just can’t help marveling at an AI assistant pulling context and information from various sources, verifying it, and executing any given task as if it were a meticulous researcher. The novelty factor alone makes it so fun to use.Besides Gemini Spark, I’ve also extensively used its direct rival, Perplexity Computer, which has been around for much longer. My experience with both tools has helped me understand how different their approaches are, and there are some meaningful ways Gemini can improve by taking a page out of Perplexity’s book.Would you trust an AI agent to handle your work?27 votesGoogle is actually the sparkGoogleOnce you start looking past the flashy, automated functions of Spark, you’ll notice that its biggest strength is actually the ecosystem it lives inside. Other AI tools connect to Google Workspace apps, such as Gmail and Drive, via APIs and MCP connectors, often requiring complex setup. Gemini Spark, on the other hand, has it easy as part of that family.
paragraph2: That means it doesn’t need any external connections to work within your Docs or to pull up any old context, and it works across supported Google services.For instance, I recently had to file a complaint with Amazon about a defective mattress they delivered. I could either do all the digging manually, spending at least 15 minutes on a needless task and breaking my workflow on a productive Monday morning — or ask Spark to do it. And you know what I chose!Gemini Spark pulled out my order details from Gmail with just the product name, dug out Amazon’s customer support email (it’s an incredibly taxing task, as brands are increasingly burying direct contact methods under infinite submenus in a bid to push you towards their AI chatbots rather than humans), and drafted a collated email with everything clearly stated. I just needed to give it a once-over and hit send.I just needed to give it a once-over and hit send.This is, of course, just a single example, but you can do a lot more complex stuff across Google services to weed out a lot of everyday digital friction. But once you step outside Google’s app ecosystem, you start seeing merit in how Perplexity Computer handles any given task.Why rely on a single LLM when you can have more?Joe Maring / Android AuthorityPerplexity doesn’t have its own large language model, so it uses third-party LLMs from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and others to answer your queries. That means Perplexity Computer serves as an orchestrator for this bouquet of powerful LLMs, delegating subtasks to the model best suited to them. In my case, it uses ChatGPT to generate high-quality images instead of Google’s Nano Banana, which has lost its edge.
paragraph3: Gemini Spark’s biggest strength — the closed-off Google ecosystem — also becomes its weakest link.And just like that, Gemini Spark’s biggest strength — the closed-off Google ecosystem — also becomes its weakest link, and that’s something I can’t reasonably expect Google to change. The company is hamstrung here as it simply can’t integrate competing models into its own products, so you’re stuck with whatever latest Gemini model is available at your disposal. Spark currently runs on top of Gemini 3.7 Flash, and I personally don’t find Google’s Flash-class models as reliable as Claude and ChatGPT in understanding and responding to my queries.That’s also evident in how Spark double-checks its own work before sharing the final results. In my experience, it let a few defects slip into the results it returned, requiring cross-checking the action in a different Google app and a bit of back-and-forth. That is not to say Perplexity Computer handles everything perfectly, but its self-assessment is evidently far more robust and is something Gemini Spark should definitely learn from.What if I live outside the ecosystem?Karandeep Singh / Android AuthorityAt the end of the day, there are only so many family vacations and birthday invitations I could ask Gemini Spark to plan for me. Its great potential would be put to better use in a more professional setting every single day. However, it’s currently missing from Google’s own business-oriented Workspace subscriptions. Perhaps regulatory requirements for enterprises are keeping Google from making Spark more widely available for businesses.
paragraph4: But whatever the reason may be, the delay is putting it further behind the competition.That is quite evident in how few third-party tools and integrations Gemini Spark (and even vanilla Gemini) support. They are dwarfed by the extensive list Perplexity has put together over the last several months. It works with professional tools from Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft 365, and even Google Workspace, among others. It’s honestly a better tool for those who live their professional life outside the Google ecosystem — at least until Gemini catches on.Gemini Spark makes the scary look friendlyKarandeep Singh / Android AuthorityYou must have deduced by now that Perplexity Computer is oriented more towards serious work where you need to run for hours and hours at the end to meet the goal you gave it. It has had a solid head start, which did indeed pay off. The tool feels much more mature and reliable than Gemini Spark when it comes to handling your tasks. Not to forget the fact that it can use several LLMs to the best of their abilities — something that’s going to remain unrivaled by Google for a very long time. You certainly won’t regret spending $200 a month on Perplexity Computer for the kind of sheer practicality and productivity it unlocks.One subconscious reason I regard Perplexity Computer as a more professional tool is how serious and borderline scary its interface appears. Think of Outlook versus Gmail. As with almost every Google product, Gemini Spark is much more user-friendly without feeling intimidating, even if it’s your first day with AI.
paragraph5: That kind of accessibility also extends to its entry price.Gemini Spark is much more user-friendly — and pocket-friendly, too.Against Perplexity Computer’s $200 subscription, Google recently made Gemini Spark available even to its Pro tier users, which means increasingly better value for money. A $20/month Google AI subscription will get you access to perhaps the most advanced version of AI that Google has ever created. If any company has the ability to make such advanced tools available to billions of end users worldwide with a flick of a switch, it’s Google.Gemini Spark does have a few rough edges around its corners, though that’s something you expect from a new product. None of my gripes with Spark are something Google can’t fix. Even the arrival of a new Gemini Pro model would give users more options and address my biggest gripe with it to a great degree. And that’s exactly where I see the most potential for Gemini Spark to become the default AI tool we mindlessly delegate tasks to across our devices.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.
bangla_paragraph1: Karandeep Singh / Android AuthorityI seriously thought this day would be far out in the future, but here we are. We already have AI assistants that can take instructions and execute a series of tasks (not just one at a time) without your supervision — it’s almost like having a human assistant.Google’s Gemini Spark is one such product. In fact, it’s one of the first of its kind to be so easily and widely accessible to end users rather than enterprises. It’s so intuitive that I instinctively gravitate towards Spark whenever I need something done within the Google ecosystem. It’s supposed to work in the background, but I just can’t help marveling at an AI assistant pulling context and information from various sources, verifying it, and executing any given task as if it were a meticulous researcher. The novelty factor alone makes it so fun to use.Besides Gemini Spark, I’ve also extensively used its direct rival, Perplexity Computer, which has been around for much longer. My experience with both tools has helped me understand how different their approaches are, and there are some meaningful ways Gemini can improve by taking a page out of Perplexity’s book.Would you trust an AI agent to handle your work?27 votesGoogle is actually the sparkGoogleOnce you start looking past the flashy, automated functions of Spark, you’ll notice that its biggest strength is actually the ecosystem it lives inside. Other AI tools connect to Google Workspace apps, such as Gmail and Drive, via APIs and MCP connectors, often requiring complex setup. Gemini Spark, on the other hand, has it easy as part of that family.
bangla_paragraph2: That means it doesn’t need any external connections to work within your Docs or to pull up any old context, and it works across supported Google services.For instance, I recently had to file a complaint with Amazon about a defective mattress they delivered. I could either do all the digging manually, spending at least 15 minutes on a needless task and breaking my workflow on a productive Monday morning — or ask Spark to do it. And you know what I chose!Gemini Spark pulled out my order details from Gmail with just the product name, dug out Amazon’s customer support email (it’s an incredibly taxing task, as brands are increasingly burying direct contact methods under infinite submenus in a bid to push you towards their AI chatbots rather than humans), and drafted a collated email with everything clearly stated. I just needed to give it a once-over and hit send.I just needed to give it a once-over and hit send.This is, of course, just a single example, but you can do a lot more complex stuff across Google services to weed out a lot of everyday digital friction. But once you step outside Google’s app ecosystem, you start seeing merit in how Perplexity Computer handles any given task.Why rely on a single LLM when you can have more?Joe Maring / Android AuthorityPerplexity doesn’t have its own large language model, so it uses third-party LLMs from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and others to answer your queries. That means Perplexity Computer serves as an orchestrator for this bouquet of powerful LLMs, delegating subtasks to the model best suited to them. In my case, it uses ChatGPT to generate high-quality images instead of Google’s Nano Banana, which has lost its edge.
bangla_paragraph3: Gemini Spark’s biggest strength — the closed-off Google ecosystem — also becomes its weakest link.And just like that, Gemini Spark’s biggest strength — the closed-off Google ecosystem — also becomes its weakest link, and that’s something I can’t reasonably expect Google to change. The company is hamstrung here as it simply can’t integrate competing models into its own products, so you’re stuck with whatever latest Gemini model is available at your disposal. Spark currently runs on top of Gemini 3.7 Flash, and I personally don’t find Google’s Flash-class models as reliable as Claude and ChatGPT in understanding and responding to my queries.That’s also evident in how Spark double-checks its own work before sharing the final results. In my experience, it let a few defects slip into the results it returned, requiring cross-checking the action in a different Google app and a bit of back-and-forth. That is not to say Perplexity Computer handles everything perfectly, but its self-assessment is evidently far more robust and is something Gemini Spark should definitely learn from.What if I live outside the ecosystem?Karandeep Singh / Android AuthorityAt the end of the day, there are only so many family vacations and birthday invitations I could ask Gemini Spark to plan for me. Its great potential would be put to better use in a more professional setting every single day. However, it’s currently missing from Google’s own business-oriented Workspace subscriptions. Perhaps regulatory requirements for enterprises are keeping Google from making Spark more widely available for businesses.

title: Musicians-turned-detectives are hunting for AI grifters
title_bn: মিউজিশিয়ান-ডিটেক্টিভরা এআই জালিয়াতিকারীদের খোঁজ করছে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: As audio-focused generative tools and platforms have gotten more sophisticated, the internet has become increasingly filled with AI-generated music whose melodies and vocals are algorithmically derived from the work of human artists. While some of th
paragraph1: As audio-focused generative tools and platforms have gotten more sophisticated, the internet has become increasingly filled with AI-generated music whose melodies and vocals are algorithmically derived from the work of human artists. While some of the people pumping out this kind of content immediately own up to using AI, others have denied using the technology until increasing public scrutiny forced them to tell the truth.For musicians — especially those creating art in technologically-focused spaces like electronic dance music — the increasingly complicated question of what is “real” and what isn’t feels particularly urgent and personal. Professional courtesy can make this only more complex; listeners can call out performers they suspect of using gen AI, but it’s something else for artists to raise concerns about their professional peers. There are some though, like 26-year-old EDM producer Max “H4RRIS” Harris, who are taking a stand against generative technology with videos calling out anyone they believe is trying to pass off AI slop as human-made art.When I recently spoke with Harris, he told me that he sees AI-generated music as “a kind of decoy art form,” and he thinks that the people making it don’t really have anything meaningful to say with their creations. He feels that true art in any medium is “created by people that are trying to express feelings and messages,” and he believes that the only thing AI boosters are really interested in is making a quick profit.“I don’t consider AI-generated material to be art, and I don’t think this technology is really advancing art in any meaningful way,” Harris said. “It’s a technological advancement that’s giving people a way to steal real art and pass it off as their own.”Harris, originally from Maine, described his approach to making music as being fairly similar to working in other creative mediums.
paragraph2: He always begins with a core concept before he starts “throwing more ideas down until I find something that sticks.” And as complicated as his workflow might look to someone unfamiliar with all of the tools and programs that he uses — his production setup includes Ableton Live, Novation Launchkey 49 MIDI controller, Ableton Push 3, Launchpad X, a couple of analog synthesizers, Serum, Diva, and the software sampler Kontakt — he said that the entire process is “really just me making creative decisions” that culminates in a sound that feels right.“Each of those decisions — and there’s hundreds of them to go into each song — brings me closer to evoking a specific kind of idea or emotion,” Harris explained. “And then once I have a song mapped out, I have to start making even more choices about how to mix it in a way that makes it sound good and presentable.”In Harris’ view, being a real artist means being able to make those kinds of experimental but informed creative decisions using your own studied understanding of a given medium. One of Harris’ biggest issues with gen AI is the way the technology often eliminates a user’s need to think about how songs (or books, films, podcasts, etc.) come together. But he has also been dismayed at the way that AI posers are muddying listeners’ understanding of what human-made EDM actually sounds like.“Aside from the similar vocals, you can usually hear a sharp hissing throughout the track,” Harris said of AI-generated songs. “I think that comes from the way that these models often work by starting with a big white noise block and then making guesses about waveforms by referencing data taken from real songs.
paragraph3: ”Harris pointed to MANSA’s “Midnight on My Mind” and Danny and Ian Asher’s “Take Me (To The Moon)” as what he thinks are examples of AI-produced songs that embody what he jokingly refers to as “the AI revolution” that’s responsible for polluting the EDM space. MANSA, Danny, and Asher have not publicly commented on whether they use generative tools in their music. But Harris and other EDM fans have noticed the similarities between “Take Me (To The Moon)” and another person’s AI-generated track. There’s no definitive evidence that MANSA produced “Midnight on My Mind” with AI. Harris could very well be wrong about these songs being generated with AI. But his insistence that they are reflects the larger culture of mistrust that has developed in response to the growing presence of AI content online.“People are just straight up uploading original, copyrighted tracks of artists like Madonna and asking [AI] to remix them.”Harris holds AI production company Suno responsible for the recent spike in this kind of music being uploaded to the internet, but he also credits specific quirks of the platform for helping him learn how to spot songs worth calling out.“Something I’ve noticed with a lot of Suno-generated tracks is that a lot of the time, you’ll hear the vocals and other melodic elements will start stuttering at the same exact time,” Harris explained. “These models still have a hard time fully separating different parts of the songs they’re trained on, and they treat these elements like one big instrument.
paragraph4: As a music producer, all of these things come across like choices that a human just wouldn’t make with their compositions because it just doesn’t make sense.”In some instances, the visuals accompanying AI tracks are part of what prompts Harris to accuse people of slinging AI. You might not be able to hear the generative models behind evangelical Christian AI persona Lionsaddle’s music, but you can clearly see the character’s fingers vanishing in and out of existence in videos. There is also an overly glossy visual quality to most of the videos posted by Christian house musician Midnite Manna that makes their content look a lot like what we typically refer to as AI slop.Suno also came up multiple times during my conversation with 39-year-old Italian turntabilist-turned-producer Nihil Young. Young’s posts on Threads about people using Suno are what initially inspired Harris to make his videos. Like Harris, Young has spent the past few months watching multiple EDM newcomers’ stars rise after they post music he thinks was generated with AI tools like Suno’s. And while Young isn’t usually one to get involved with online discourse, he felt it was important to speak out about how many people are flooding the scene with AI tracks.“These songs are the sound of Suno, which to me means that the people behind the songs are just straight up uploading original, copyrighted tracks of artists like Madonna and asking the platform to remix them,” Young told me, referring to Josh Fawaz’s “Like a Prayer” cover, which now includes AI credits following a wave of online backlash. “If they can do it with major artists like her, they can do it with you, me, and everyone else, which just isn’t cool.
paragraph5: They can take your entire catalog, feed it to Suno, and generate ‘new’ songs from that stolen work.”Young claimed that in response to his Threads posts, he received multiple hacking attempts and a wave of online harassment from AI defenders. He also told me that he thinks people bought fake followers to boost his Spotify numbers as a way of casting doubt on his authenticity. That spooked Young — who is raising a young daughter and just put out a new album of his own — to rethink whether he should continue. He’s taken a break from callouts, but he still thinks it’s important to know about the way AI music is harming human artists.“Music production is where most of my income comes from, and almost as soon as AI began rolling out, I started losing many of my clients,” said Young, who has previously done audio mixing and mastering work for Sony Music, Warner, and Universal. “I can only imagine what it’s been like for singers, graphics artists, and people working in other creative fields. Whether you realize it or not, this stuff is impacting everyone.”What Young wishes more listeners could appreciate is how easy it has become to generate entire songs with platforms like Suno.
bangla_paragraph1: অডিও-ফোকাসযুক্ত জেনারেটিভ সরঞ্জাম এবং প্ল্যাটফর্মগুলি আরও পরিশীলিত হয়ে উঠার সাথে সাথে ইন্টারনেট আরও বেশি করে এআই-উত্পাদিত সংগীতে পরিপূর্ণ হয়ে উঠেছে যার সুর এবং কণ্ঠস্বরগুলি অ্যালগরিদমিকভাবে মানব শিল্পীদের কাজ থেকে উদ্ভূত। যদিও এই ধরণের সামগ্রীগুলি পাম্প করা কিছু লোক অবিলম্বে এআই ব্যবহারের স্বীকারোক্তি দেয়, অন্যরা প্রযুক্তি ব্যবহার করতে অস্বীকার করেছে যতক্ষণ না ক্রমবর্ধমান জনসাধারণের তদারকি তাদের সত্য বলতে বাধ্য করে।
bangla_paragraph2: তিনি সবসময় একটি মূল ধারণা দিয়ে শুরু করেন তার আগে তিনি আরও ধারণা নিক্ষেপ করা শুরু করেন যতক্ষণ না আমি এমন কিছু খুঁজে পাই যা আটকে যায়। এবং যতই জটিল তার কর্মপ্রবাহ তার ব্যবহার করা সমস্ত সরঞ্জাম এবং প্রোগ্রামগুলির সাথে পরিচিত না হওয়া ব্যক্তির কাছে দেখা যেতে পারে  তার উত্পাদন সেটআপটিতে অ্যাবলটন লাইভ, নভেশন লঞ্চকি 49 মিডি কন্ট্রোলার, অ্যাবলটন পুশ 3, লঞ্চপ্যাড এক্স, একটি অ্যানালগ সিনথেসাইজার, সিরাম, ডিভা এবং সফ্টওয়্যার স্যাম্পলার যোগাযোগ  তিনি বলেছিলেন যে পুরো প্রক্রিয়াটি সত্যিই সৃজনশীল সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণের জন্য কেবল আমি
bangla_paragraph3: হ্যারিস ম্যানসা মিডনাইট অন মাই মিন্ড এবং ড্যানি এবং ইয়ান অ্যাশার টেক মি (টু দ্য মুন)  এর দিকে ইঙ্গিত দিয়েছিলেন যে তিনি যা ভাবেন তা এআই-উত্পাদিত গানের উদাহরণ যা তিনি কৌতুকের সাথে যা উল্লেখ করেন তা অন্তর্নিহিত করে এআই বিপ্লব যা ইডিএম স্থানকে দূষিত করার জন্য দায়ী। ম্যানজা, ড্যানী এবং অ্যাশর তাদের সংগীতে প্রজনন সরঞ্জাম ব্যবহার করে কিনা তা নিয়ে প্রকাশ্যে মন্তব্য করেননি। তবে হ্যারিসের এবং অন্যান্য ইডিএমের অনুরাগীরা মেক মি [টু দ্যা মুন]  এবং অন্য ব্যক্তির এআই উত্পন্ন ট্র্যাকের মধ্যে মিল লক্ষ্য করেছেন।
bangla_paragraph4: একটি সঙ্গীত প্রযোজক হিসাবে, এই সমস্ত জিনিসগুলি এমন পছন্দগুলির মতো দেখাচ্ছে যা কোনও মানুষ তাদের রচনাগুলির সাথে করবে না কারণ এটি কেবল অর্থহীন। কিছু ক্ষেত্রে, এআই ট্র্যাকগুলির সাথে থাকা ভিজ্যুয়ালগুলি হ্যারিসকে এআই-র স্লিংয়ের জন্য লোকদের অভিযুক্ত করার জন্য প্ররোচিত করে। আপনি ইভেঞ্জেলিকাল খ্রিস্টান এআই পার্সোনাল লিওনস্যাডল এর সংগীতের পিছনে উত্পাদনশীল মডেলগুলি শুনতে সক্ষম নাও হতে পারেন, তবে আপনি স্পষ্টভাবে দেখতে পারেন যে চরিত্রের আঙ্গুলগুলি ভিডিওতে অদৃশ্য হয়ে যায়।
bangla_paragraph5: তারা আপনার পুরো ক্যাটালগটি নিতে পারে, এটি সুনোকে ফিড করতে পারে এবং সেই চুরি করা কাজ থেকে নতুন  গান তৈরি করতে পারে।  ইয়ং দাবি করেছিলেন যে তার থ্রেডস পোস্টের জবাবে তিনি একাধিক হ্যাকিংয়ের প্রচেষ্টা এবং এআই প্রতিরক্ষীদের কাছ থেকে অনলাইন হয়রানির তরঙ্গ পেয়েছিলেন। তিনি আমাকে আরও বলেছিলেন যে তিনি মনে করেন যে লোকেরা তার সত্যতা নিয়ে সন্দেহের ছড়িয়ে দেওয়ার উপায় হিসাবে তার স্পটিফাই নম্বর বাড়ানোর জন্য ভুয়া অনুসারীদের কিনেছেন। এটি ইয়াংকে ভয় দেখিয়েছিল  যিনি একটি ছোট মেয়েকে বড় করছেন এবং কেবল নিজের একটি নতুন অ্যালবাম প্রকাশ করেছেন  পুনর্বিবেচনা করতে হবে কিনা

excerpt: Earlier this week, Meta agreed to pay approximately $18 Bn to settle lawsuits brought by a bipartisan group of 52…
paragraph1: SUMMARYMeta will pay approximately $18 Bn and introduce stricter safeguards for teenage Facebook and Instagram users in participating US jurisdictions The safeguards show Meta can redesign its platforms to protect teenagers, raising questions about why similar protections are not being extended to India and other markets India is exploring age-based social media restrictions, while experts are calling for age-appropriate product design, stronger age-assurance systems, and greater platform accountability Earlier this week, Meta agreed to pay approximately $18 Bn to settle lawsuits brought by a bipartisan group of 52 attorneys general from US states, territories, and the District of Columbia over allegations that Facebook and Instagram harmed children and teenagers. But the more consequential part of the settlement may not be the money. Meta has also agreed to change how its platforms work for users below 18 in participating US jurisdictions. The measures include a default two-hour daily limit across Facebook and Instagram, restrictions on access between midnight and 6 AM, muted notifications during school hours, stronger parental controls and age-assurance systems, and the option to use a non-algorithmic feed. The usage limit can only be disabled with parental permission, although direct messages are exempt from the usage, Night Mode, and School Mode restrictions. Meta will also restrict cosmetic surgery and extreme makeup filters and hide visible like counts by default. Most of the measures will remain in place for 10 years, although the usage limit and Night Mode initially carry a five-year commitment. These restrictions will become stricter and extend to 10 years if TikTok and YouTube adopt comparable safeguards. Meta has not admitted wrongdoing as part of the settlement. Crucially, the agreement applies only in participating US states and territories. Meta has not committed to introducing the same package globally. In response to Inc42’s queries on whether it plans to extend these safeguards to India and other markets, among other issues, Meta directed Inc42 to its blog post announcing the settlement.
paragraph2: The post did not address the company’s plans for extending the measures beyond participating US jurisdictions. For India, this distinction matters. The Centre is already scrutinising Meta over child sexual abuse material (CSAM), deepfakes, unlabelled AI-generated content, and content moderation. The government is also exploring age-based restrictions on social media. The settlement offers Indian regulators a ready reference for moving beyond content moderation and examining how social media products are designed for children. India’s Child Safety Gap The settlement comes as governments worldwide tighten controls on children’s use of social media. Australia requires covered platforms to prevent children under 16 from holding accounts, while several European countries are considering age restrictions and stronger age-assurance requirements. India has yet to settle on a national framework. Karnataka has proposed restricting social media use by children below 16, while Andhra Pradesh is considering restrictions for those below 13. The Centre has also held discussions with social media companies and may favour a graded framework based on age rather than a blanket ban. As the country develops its approach, legal and industry experts see little justification for offering Indian children a lower baseline of protection merely because regulators have not yet mandated stricter safeguards. RECOMMENDED FOR yOU “There is no persuasive reason why a safety feature considered necessary for a 15-year-old in California should be unavailable to a 15-year-old in Delhi,” said Software Freedom Law Center founder Mishi Choudhary.
paragraph3: Mayank Arora, a Delhi-based lawyer and partner at Chambers of Bharat Chugh, agreed that children should receive similar protections across markets. If particular product features warrant usage limits, night-time restrictions, age assurance, and parental controls in one market, platforms should provide a comparable level of protection globally, he said. However, Mohammad Faisal Kawoosa of Techarc believes India should develop safeguards suited to its social and cultural environment. “I wouldn’t say India must have the same measures. But, yes, we must have measures in place to safeguard our children on digital platforms that suit our requirements as well as cultural framework,” Kawoosa said. When Product Design Causes Harm The settlement shifts the debate beyond content moderation and towards product design – whether Facebook and Instagram are built to protect teenagers from excessive use and other risks. While social media safety debates have traditionally focused on the removal of CSAM, deepfakes, bullying, and other harmful content, the agreement raises questions about usage limits, notification timings, infinite recommendations, beauty filters, and visible like counts. These are product decisions, not merely content moderation decisions. Satish Meena, founder of Datum Intelligence, believes this is where the gap in India’s regulatory framework becomes apparent. “There is no Indian rule on default settings, notification timing, or which engagement features can be shown to a minor account,” he said. Features such as beauty filters, infinite scroll, and recommendation systems may not necessarily involve the collection of a child’s personal data, but they can still influence how young users behave and perceive themselves. This raises a broader question for regulators: should platforms be required to design safer products for children instead of merely complying with rules governing their data?
paragraph4: Arora believes India should adopt a graded framework based on age. “An eight-year-old or a 13-year-old cannot be treated as having the same levels of maturity and digital autonomy,” he said. What Should India Demand? The settlement does not create a judicial precedent because Meta settled the cases without admitting wrongdoing. However, it could still influence regulators elsewhere by demonstrating that Meta can impose usage limits, restrict overnight access, change default recommendations, and strengthen age-assurance systems. The debate is already taking shape in India. The IT ministry recently held discussions with Meta over CSAM, deepfakes, and content moderation, and sought stronger systems to identify and remove harmful material. Officials have also raised concerns about human oversight, particularly for content in Indian languages. For India, the bigger question is what happens when platforms face similar concerns here. “In India, we have repeatedly settled for an apology,” said Ritesh Bhatia, founder of V4WEB Cybersecurity. “When Meta’s CEO made a false statement about our elections, we asked for an apology, we got one, and the file was closed. More recently, when our own parliamentary panel raised serious concerns about child sexual abuse material and deepfakes on the platform, the outcome was again reported to be an apology.
paragraph5: ” Bhatia argued that the contrast with the US was stark: 52 attorneys general pursued Meta in federal court and secured billions of dollars in payments alongside enforceable product changes for children. “An apology costs Meta nothing. A penalty costs it something,” he said. India could introduce age-appropriate defaults, regulate features available to minor accounts, strengthen age assurance, and impose penalties for non-compliance. The pressure could also extend beyond Meta. Around $5.3 Bn of its settlement payment is conditional on TikTok and YouTube introducing prescribed safeguards and making matching payments. If they agree, Meta’s daily limit will fall to one hour per app, while Night Mode will expand to 10 PM–7 AM. But even industry-wide adoption in the US would leave the question of geographical parity unresolved.

title: Grand Theft Auto 6 will run at only 30 FPS on consoles at launch, no performance mode promised — even the souped-up PS5 Pro might not get 60 FPS support
title_bn: গ্র্যান্ড চুরি অটো ৬ লঞ্চের সময় কনসোলে মাত্র ৩০ FPS এ চলবে, কোন পারফরম্যান্স মোডের প্রতিশ্রুতি নেই  এমনকি সুপ আপ করা PS5 প্রোও ৬০ FPS সমর্থন নাও পেতে পারে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: GTA 6 is currently running at 30 FPS at Rockstar internally with no confirmation on a 60 FPS mode being available at launch, or even later.
paragraph1: (Image credit: Rockstar Games) It's almost hard to believe that Grand Theft Auto VI is finally almost here after years of waiting. Even more surreal was seeing the first official gameplay reveal happen only three months before launch, which came with an inevitable update: GTA 6 will be locked to 30 FPS. YouTuber Davy Jones was invited by Rockstar North for a three-hour gameplay showcase where leadership confirmed the game does not target 60 FPS at launch. GTA 6, o NOVO TRAILER, Extended Look Oficial - YouTube Watch On Head of Development at Rockstar North, Rob Nelson, played the game for 2+ hours in front of Jones, who then detailed the experience on his Flow Games podcast. He said he could see the game running at 30 FPS during the demonstration, so he inquired about performance modes.
paragraph2: Nelson replied that the game runs at 30 FPS for now, and that he'd need to "consult the technical team" for whether we'll see 60 FPS at launch "or later."This has been the standard for Rockstar games for more than a decade at this point — release the game with a 30 FPS target in mind and update it later with a 60 FPS patch on more performant hardware. GTA V runs at 30 FPS on both the PS3 and PS4, but got updated to run at 60 FPS on the PS5. Red Dead Redemption 2 is unfortunately still stuck at 60 FPS on even current-gen consoles, however.Following that track record, we likely won't see 60 FPS support on consoles till the PS7, while PC will enjoy unlocked frame rates once its port drops down the line.
paragraph3: Digital Foundry expounded upon the 30 FPS limitation, theorizing that the high NPC density, dynamic weather, physics simulation, and advanced traffic AI will be too much for a console's CPU to handle. The GPU is not the bottleneck, because otherwise the PS5 Pro wouldn't have an issue pushing 60 FPS.Nelson didn't confirm anything about performance modes either, which gives further credence to the PS5 Pro assumption. Rockstar also remained tight-lipped about what resolution we can expect across the different consoles; Digital Foundry says yesterday's presentation ran at upscaled 4K (from 1440p). The Xbox Series S is considerably slower than the base PS5 and Xbox Series X, while the PS5 Pro packs a lot more grunt, along with PSSR 2 for upscaling.
paragraph4: (Image credit: Rockstar Games)The same goes for other details like ray tracing, though it's widely speculated that GTA VI is relying on ray-traced reflections and lighting, which will likely improve in quality on the PS5 Pro, implying that Rockstar is prioritizing graphics over raw framerates. The gameplay released yesterday was captured on the base PS5. While the visual fidelity was on-point, keen-eyed viewers were able to notice the intense motion blur used in some scenes.The car chase with the police particularly stands out because the fast-moving gameplay had visible smears and subtle streaking across different elements while the interwoven cutscenes did not. It seems like motion blur will be required to make the game feel smoother than it really is; besides, it can't be turned off on consoles anyway.
paragraph5: Perhaps a 40 FPS mode could serve as a middle-ground tradeoff for 120 Hz VRR displays.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds. Hassam Nasir is a die-hard hardware enthusiast with years of experience as a tech editor and writer, focusing on detailed CPU comparisons and general hardware news. When he’s not working, you’ll find him bending tubes for his ever-evolving custom water-loop gaming rig or benchmarking the latest CPUs and GPUs just for fun.

title: Deco Gear DG49OLED240 49-inch 32:9 OLED gaming monitor review: Two 27-inch QHD screens without the dividing line
title_bn: ডেকো গিয়ার ডিজি 49OLED240 49 ইঞ্চি 32:9 ওএলইডি গেমিং মনিটর পর্যালোচনাঃ বিভক্ত লাইন ছাড়াই দুটি 27 ইঞ্চির কিউএইচডি স্ক্রিন
author: TechPulse
excerpt: You can replace two 27-inch QHD monitors with one Deco Gear DG49OLED240. This 49-inch 32:9 QD-OLED panel has an 1800R curve, 240 Hz, 5120x1440 pixels, HDR10, DisplayHDR 400, wide gamut color, and Adaptive-Sync.
paragraph1: If you already have two screens and can’t stand the dividing line, or you want to double your screen area from the 27-inch QHD monitor you’re currently running, the Deco Gear DG49OLED240 is a no-brainer. It delivers addictive gaming with smooth performance and a stunning image. Pros +Addictive gaming performance with perfect smoothness and low input lag +Stunning image with deep contrast and balanced color +Accurate color out of the box +Audio quality that’s well above the norm +A perfect replacement for dual 27-inch QHD display Cons -Unintuitive OSD with unusual controls -Slightly dark gamma Why you can trust Tom's Hardware Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test. Go to page: Few, if any, users will say that they have too much screen real estate. There’s always one more window you’d like to open, or you’ll often wish you could see just a little more of a game environment. To this end, many people run two or three of the best gaming monitors together. This approach solves many problems, and if you go for something common like a 27-inch QHD, the price isn’t too high. But there’s one thing you can’t escape: the dividing line.Monitors always have a frame; even the flush ones are visible. And no one will say that they like the line. It can perhaps be ignored, but it doesn’t just magically disappear. The simplest solution is to go for an ultra-wide display. If you’re currently running two 27-inch QHD monitors, you can replace them with a single 49-inch 32:9 panel. Add a curve, and you have a screen that’s great for productivity, gaming, and simulation.This isn’t necessarily the least expensive solution, but if you buy one from Deco Gear, you can put the DG49OLED240 on your desk for $1,230. That will get you 5120x1440 pixels, a Quantum Dot OLED panel, 240 Hz, Adaptive-Sync, HDR400, and wide gamut color. Let’s take a look. Swipe to scroll horizontally Panel Type / Backlight Quantum Dot Organic Light Emitting Diode (QD-OLED) Screen Size / Aspect Ratio 49 inches / 32:9 Row 2 - Cell 0 Curve radius: 1800mm Max Resolution and Refresh Rate 5120x1440 @ 240 Hz Row 4 - Cell 0 FreeSync and G-Sync Compatible Native Color Depth and Gamut 10-bit / DCI-P3+ Row 6 - Cell 0 HDR10, DisplayHDR 400 Response Time (GTG) 0.03ms Brightness (mfr) 250 nits SDR Row 9 - Cell 0 400 nits HDR Contrast Unmeasurable Speakers 2x 5w + 1x 10w Video Inputs 2x DisplayPort 1.
paragraph2: 4 Row 13 - Cell 0 1x HDMI 2.1, 1x USB-C Audio 3.5mm headphone output USB 3.0 1x up, 2x down or None Power Consumption 71w, brightness @ 200 nits Panel Dimensions WxHxD w/base 47.2 x 17.6-22.2 x 14.2 inches (735 x 447-564 x 240mm) Panel Thickness 6.7 inches (170mm) Bezel Width Top/sides: 0.47 inch (12mm) Row 20 - Cell 0 Bottom: 0.59 inch (15mm) Weight 20.9 pounds (9.5kg) Warranty 1 year The 49-inch 32:9 display format is the exact equivalent of two 27-inch 16:9 QHD screens; it’s the perfect solution for those who would otherwise run two monitors. The only downside is that it costs more than two 27-inch QHD panels. But given the specs in play here, the DG49OLED240 delivers a lot for the money.With Quantum Dot color, you get a healthy 112% coverage of DCI-P3. That’s more than many 34-inch 21:9 screens I’ve reviewed. It’s reasonably accurate out of the box as well. My sample measured well before calibration and better after a few adjustments.Light output is around 430 nits for SDR and HDR content.
paragraph3: That’s with variable brightness engaged and measurement of a 25% window pattern. Full field white comes in around 360 nits. The DG49OLED240 provides more than enough brightness for impactful HDR in an indoor space with some ambient light. It also plays well in the dark with lower levels that maintain full color and contrast.Video processing is excellent in all respects with a 240 Hz refresh rate and Adaptive-Sync. I measured panel response on par with other OLEDs and lower input lag than other 49-inch 32:9 screens in my test database.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Gaming is enhanced by a pair of internal five-watt speakers accompanied by a 10-watt woofer plus a 3.5mm headphone jack. And you can hang those cans on a stout metal hook that flips out from the stand. Video inputs include two DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, and a USB-C that includes 90 watts of charging power. Additional USB ports support things like input devices and webcams. You also get LED lighting in the back with control in the OSD.If you’re wondering about the Deco Gear brand, it is a subsidiary of Beach Camera, a very experienced vendor of electronics and technology. You can buy the DG49OLED240 directly for $1,229.99, or in one of Beach Camera’s brick-and-mortar locations.Assembly and AccessoriesThe DG49OLED240 showed up in a large white carton with just the words “49” OLED Ultrawide Monitor” printed on it. A visit to Deco Gear’s website revealed that several variants of this display differ mainly by refresh rate.
paragraph4: The DG49OLED240 is the flagship model at 240 Hz. The contents are packed in crumbly foam and assembled tool-free. The accessory bundle includes an IEC cord for the internal power supply plus DisplayPort, HDMI and USB cables.Product 360 Image 1 of 4 (Image credit: Deco Gear) The DG49OLED240 is styled simply with just a Deco Gear logo on the front, screened on above a small protrusion. This is where you’ll find the only control, a tiny joystick. It covers all monitor functions. A word of warning: pressing it only toggles power. It doesn’t select functions like every other joystick on every other monitor. So, unless you plan to turn the DG49OLED240 on or off, do not press it.The screen’s bezel is flush so you can’t see it when the power’s off. But it is a tad wider than average at 12mm around the top and sides and 15mm at the bottom. In practice though, you’ll be so glad to get rid of the line down the center after chucking your two 27-inch screens that you won’t care.The stand is super solid with a wide and deep base made from cast aluminum and finished in a matte black powdercoat. It’s almost monolithic, but there is a bit of wobble where the panel snaps on. This is typical of super wide monitors. Ergonomics include a 4.6-inch height range plus 5/20 degrees tilt and 20 degrees swivel.In the back are LED lights in two vertical arrays that frame the rear-facing I/O panel. There are two DisplayPort 1.4s and an HDMI 2.
paragraph5: 1. A USB-C handles video signals and provides 90 watts of power. There are USB ports too, one upstream and two downstream. A 3.5mm headphone jack delivers audio, and there’s an RJ-45 network port.OSD FeaturesThe DG49OLED240’s OSD is somewhat frustrating to control because the joystick doesn’t work the same way as nearly every other monitor I’ve encountered. One major issue I had was that pressing it toggles the power no matter what menu you’re currently in. I lost count of how many times I accidentally turned off my review sample. To select a function, right-click. To back out of the menu, left-click. Once I got the hang of it, I was able to find everything I needed for image control and video processing. Image 1 of 5 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Every menu screen has basic signal information at the top in three small portholes. The menu graphics are game-focused with a purposeful red border on a black background. Game Settings is up first with four image modes, an Adaptive-Sync toggle, and Shadow Balance, which brightens darker areas for better visibility. On the second screen, you get a frame counter, two aiming points, and a timer. Dynamic Brightness is a global dimming feature. HDR can be turned off or engaged with two different modes. Ambient Lighting refers to the LEDs on the back.
